activities.title: Write About the Park
activities.skill: Describe a picture with simple sentences
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the park. Write 1 or 2 sentences. Tell what you see and what the children are doing. You can write on paper too.
activities.prompt: Look at the picture of the park. What do you see? What are the children doing?

picture.alt: A sunny park with a tree, a girl on a swing, a boy kicking a red ball, a brown dog, and a bench.

activities.responsePlaceholder: I see a ___. The girl is ___.

models.A: I see a park. A girl is on the swing.
models.B: A girl swings beside a tree. A boy kicks a red ball.
models.C: Beside the tree, a girl is swinging while a boy kicks a red ball nearby.

vocabulary: park
an outdoor place with grass, trees, and things to play on
parque: un lugar al aire libre con pasto, árboles y juegos
swing
a seat on ropes or chains that moves back and forth
columpio: un asiento colgado que se mueve hacia adelante y hacia atrás
kick
to hit something with your foot
patear: golpear algo con el pie
writeFor: tells what one person is doing (is + -ing)
a capital letter and a period
activities.correct: Nice describing! You named things in the picture and told what someone is doing.
activities.hint: Point to one person. What is that person doing? Write: The ___ is ___ing.
activities.support: Use I see ___. Then use The girl is ___ or The boy is ___.
activities.extension: Add a color word: The boy is kicking a red ball.

teacher.use: Picture description warm-up; works as a paper booklet item.
teacher.function: Inform — naming objects and actions with is + -ing.
teacher.lower: Students label 3 things in the picture first, then copy one frame.
teacher.onLevel: Expect 1–2 sentences that name objects and one action.
teacher.challenge: Ask for three sentences using also and and.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture; students write under it on lined paper.
teacher.prompt: What is one more thing happening in the park?

successCriteria: Name something visible in the park.
Tell what a child is doing.
Add an accurate detail, such as color or location. One or two clear sentences are enough.

modelNotes.A: Names the place and tells where a child is.
modelNotes.B: Uses precise action words—swings and kicks—and the visible color red.
modelNotes.C: Connects two visible actions with while and adds location. It is one sentence: quality does not require a longer answer.

activities.title: Picture Story: The Seed
activities.skill: Narrate a three-picture story with first, next, last
activities.directions: Look at the three pictures. Write what happens first, next, and last. Use the words first, next, and last.
activities.prompt: Look at the three pictures. What happens to the seed? Tell the story in order.

picture.alt: Three panels: 1) a girl puts a seed in a pot of soil, 2) she waters the pot and a small sprout grows, 3) a tall yellow flower blooms in the pot and she smiles.

models.A: She puts a seed in a pot. The flower grows.
models.B: First, the girl puts a seed in a pot of soil. Then she waters the pot, and a little sprout comes up. Last, a tall yellow flower grows, and she is happy because her seed grew.
models.C: A girl grew a beautiful flower from one tiny seed. First, she pressed the seed into a pot of soil. Next, she watered it every day, and soon a small green sprout popped up. After a few weeks, a tall yellow flower opened in the sun. She smiled because her hard work helped the seed grow into a plant.

vocabulary: seed
a tiny thing that grows into a plant
semilla: una cosa pequeña que crece y se convierte en planta
water
to give a plant water
regar: darle agua a una planta
grow
to get bigger
crecer: hacerse más grande
writeFor: action words like puts, waters, grows
activities.correct: Great story! You told the three parts in order with first, next, and last.
activities.hint: Look at picture 1 and write one sentence. Then do picture 2 and picture 3.
activities.support: One picture = one sentence. Start each sentence with first, next, or last.
activities.extension: Add how the girl feels at the end: She feels ___ because ___.

teacher.use: Picture-sequence narrative like the ACCESS booklet task.
teacher.function: Narrate — time-order words and past or present action verbs.
teacher.lower: Students say each panel aloud, then write with the three frames.
teacher.onLevel: Expect three ordered sentences with sequence words.
teacher.challenge: Add a feeling and a reason at the end.
teacher.noTech: Print the three panels; students write under each panel.
teacher.prompt: What does a seed need to grow?

successCriteria: Address the task: Look at the three pictures. What happens to the seed? Tell the story in order.
Put the events or steps in an order the reader or listener can follow.
Include a relevant action or detail at each important step.

activities.title: Pick a Class Pet
activities.skill: Give an opinion with a reason
activities.directions: Look at the two pictures. Which class pet is better, the fish or the hamster? Write your choice and one reason.
activities.prompt: Look at the two pictures. Which pet should our class get? Why?

activities.responsePlaceholder: I think the ___ is better because ___.

models.A: I like the fish. It is pretty.
models.B: I think our class should get the hamster. I like it because it is soft and fun to watch. It runs on the wheel, so it is never boring.
models.C: Our class should get a goldfish as a class pet. First, a fish is quiet, so it will not bother us when we read or take tests. Also, it only needs a little food each day and a clean tank. A hamster is cute, but it can bite and needs more care. For these reasons, a goldfish is the best pet for our classroom.

activities.support: An opinion tells what you think. Because tells why.
